sections.h2: Who handles property tax matters in Knox County?
sections.html:
A seller in Knox County will typically touch three offices. The County Treasurer, based in the courthouse in Galesburg, mails the bills and takes the money. The county Assessment Office, 309-345-3845, runs exemptions and hands out Board of Review forms. Township assessors set the values. Tax sale certificates and redemption sit with the County Clerk.

Assessing is split three ways. One assessor covers the North District: Rio, Ontario, Walnut Grove, Lynn, Henderson, Sparta, Copley, Victoria, Persifer and Truro townships. Another covers the South District: Galesburg, Knox, Cedar, Orange, Haw Creek, Elba, Indian Point, Chestnut, Maquon and Salem. The City of Galesburg township has a separate assessor of its own, so the right call depends on the parcel's location.

sections.h2: How large is Knox County and what do homes sell for?
sections.html:
Knox County takes in 716 square miles of land in west central Illinois, and Galesburg is both the seat and the biggest city. Fulton County gave up land to create it in 1825. It borders Mercer, Henry, Stark, Peoria, Fulton and Warren Counties. Among the ten school districts are Galesburg CUSD 205, Knoxville CUSD 202 and ROWVA CUSD 208.

The population is sliding: 49,967 in the 2020 count and an estimated 47,767 in July 2025. Census figures for 2020 through 2024 show a $111,900 median home value, 70.8% of households owning their homes and a median income of $57,030. One building permit was issued in 2025, and 23.9% of residents are 65 or older.

Where values are this low, a modest bill still eats a real share of a house's worth, so look at the assessment before you list.

sections.h2: What are the Knox County tax due dates and late penalties?
sections.html:
Taxes for the 2025 tax year were payable in 2026 on two dates, July 1 and September 1. Both dates have passed. Knox County mails one bill a year with a detachable stub for each installment, so check the dates printed on the current bill or ask the Treasurer.

Knox County late penalty on 2025 taxes payable in 2026 (source: Knox County Treasurer, Important Dates)
DateFirst installmentSecond installment
July 2, 20261.50%Not yet due
August 2, 20263.00%Not yet due
September 2, 20264.50%1.50%
October 2, 20266.00%3.00%
November 2, 20267.50%4.50%

Per the Treasurer, the charge is 1.5% each month, applies in full rather than by the day, and begins the morning after a due date. Not getting a bill does not excuse the tax (35 ILCS 200/20-15).

sections.h2: Where can you pay a Knox County tax bill?
sections.html:
The Treasurer offers several ways to pay, and the detachable stub has to go with the payment:

  • Send a check or deliver it to the Treasurer's Office, made out to Knox County Collector; a mailed check's cancelled copy is your receipt
  • Leave a check in a courthouse drop box, one on Tompkins Street by the north curb and one at the parking lot exit, with no envelopes supplied
  • Take it to a local bank in the county (Wells Fargo is excluded at its own request)
  • Use a credit or debit card and pay a fee of 2.35%, with a $2.95 minimum

A postmark counts if the payment goes out before the tax sale. Drop box items collected at 8:30 each morning are posted to the day before. Where a lender pays from escrow, the county puts the duty of watching those payments on the owner.

sections.h2: How is a Knox County assessment determined?
sections.html:
Assessors value property as of each January 1, aiming for 33.33% of fair cash value and drawing on three years of sales; the 2026 roll used 2023 through 2025. Equalization factors follow. In 2026 they were 1.0724 in Galesburg Township, 1.0758 for the City of Galesburg, 1.0132 in Rio, Walnut Grove, Henderson and Persifer, and 1.0125 in Ontario, Sparta and Copley. Lynn, Truro, Victoria, Elba and Salem were general assessment townships that year.

The county's formula for a bill takes the final equalized assessed value, subtracts exemptions, and multiplies what remains by the tax rate. To test your own figure, divide the assessment by 0.3333 and compare that with a realistic sale price.

Before the 2026 adjustments, the three-year median assessment level measured 32.92% in the North District, 31.08% in the South District and 31.76% in the City of Galesburg, which is why the factors above push values upward. Farmland follows a separate state formula, and its factor was 1.00.

sections.h2: What is the Knox County assessment appeal process?
sections.html:
First talk to the township assessor. If that does not settle it, put a written appeal in front of the Board of Review. It must argue the property's value, not the size of the tax. Knox County's 2026 filing period ran September 17 through October 19, 2026, ending at 4 p.m., and it is over. Each year brings new forms, and older ones are refused.

  • Support the appeal with facts, such as an independent appraisal or sales of comparable homes
  • The Board answers with a notice carrying an informal decision
  • To contest it, return your acceptance of a formal hearing within ten days of the notice
  • Thirty days after a final Board decision is the limit for going to the Property Tax Appeal Board

The Board of Review meets as needed rather than on a fixed calendar. For the current forms and window, call the Assessment Office.

sections.h2: What exemptions apply to a Knox County home?
sections.html:
Exemption forms and instructions live on the county's assessment pages, and the Treasurer's page summarizes the main ones:

  • Owner-occupied homestead: a reduction of up to $6,000 in equalized assessed value
  • Senior homestead for owners 65 and older: $5,000 off
  • Senior assessment freeze: holds the taxable value for owners 65 and older; the Treasurer lists household income of $65,000 or less, and the assessment office shows $75,000 for 2026
  • Home improvement: assessed value of up to $25,000 exempt for four years

Other exemptions cover returning veterans, disabled persons and disabled veterans. Applications are requested by September 30 yearly and accepted until December 31. A buyer who moves in should contact the assessment office after the next January 1 to confirm the exemption is on the parcel.

sections.h2: What happens to delinquent Knox County taxes?
sections.html:
Knox County runs one tax sale a year, usually in mid-November, and every delinquent tax is offered. A list of delinquent taxes is printed in local newspapers each mid-October. Beginning with the 2025 taxes payable in 2026, the county chose under Public Act 104-0553 to acquire all delinquent real estate taxes itself as trustee for the taxing districts. That trustee then auctions parcels it has taken to deed.

Tax sale certificates are handled by the County Clerk's Office, 309-345-6753. The Treasurer will not give legal advice about delinquent taxes. Anyone who sells with tax outstanding should ask the Treasurer what is owed and settle it at closing.

faqs.q: What dates does Knox County collect real estate tax?
faqs.a: The 2025 taxes payable in 2026 were due July 1 and September 1, 2026. The Treasurer mails one annual bill with a stub for each installment, so read the dates on your own bill.

faqs.q: What late fee does Knox County charge?
faqs.a: The Treasurer adds 1.5% per month to the unpaid amount, with no proration, starting the day after a due date.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 Knox County appeal period still open?
faqs.a: No. It ran from September 17 to October 19, 2026, and the Board of Review may not accept complaints afterward. Call the Assessment Office at 309-345-3845 about the next window.

faqs.q: Where do I send a Knox County property tax payment?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's Office in the Knox County courthouse in Galesburg takes mail and walk-in payments. Drop boxes, most local banks and card payments are also options, and checks go to the Knox County Collector.

faqs.q: When does Knox County hold the tax sale?
faqs.a: It is usually held in mid-November, following a mid-October newspaper list of delinquent taxes. The County Clerk handles the certificates.
